title: Culture Change
description: Changing engineering culture through incentives, rituals, role modeling, and **operating mechanisms** rather than slogans.

competency.name: Culture Change
competency.definition: Diagnoses behavior patterns and changes the incentives, rituals, and leadership actions that sustain culture.
competency.whyItMatters: Culture is what the organization repeats under pressure; senior leaders must change behavior, not just messaging.

prompt.primary: Tell me about a time you intentionally changed engineering culture.
variants: Describe a time when the existing culture was blocking business or technical progress.
Tell me about a time you moved a team away from heroics toward sustainable execution.
interviewerIntent: Can the candidate diagnose culture through behavior?
Do they change incentives and rituals rather than slogans?
Can they sustain the change under pressure?

scenario.signatureExample: A CTO finds a culture of heroic firefighting and shifts recognition toward prevention, operational excellence, documentation, and sustainable delivery.
context: Teams are exhausted and reliability is uneven.
constraints: The existing culture has produced some short-term success.
Recognition and planning systems must change together.

storyAnatomy.situation: Engineering had a hero culture that rewarded firefighting more than prevention.
storyAnatomy.task: Shift the culture toward sustainable delivery and operational excellence.
action: Named the behavior pattern and its cost in incidents, burnout, and missed learning.
Changed recognition to highlight prevention, documentation, and durable fixes.
Added operational excellence goals to planning and reviews.
Coached leaders to stop rewarding avoidable heroics.
result: Teams invested more in prevention and reliability work.
Incident reviews focused more on durable fixes.
Recognition became aligned with sustainable engineering behavior.
storyAnatomy.reflection: The lesson was that culture changes when repeated leadership signals and **operating mechanisms** change together.

exampleStories.title: Heroics To Prevention
exampleStories.promptVariant: Tell me about a time you intentionally changed engineering culture.
exampleStories.situation: The organization celebrated engineers who saved launches at the last minute, while prevention, documentation, and operational excellence were invisible.
strongAnswerSketch: Name the behavior pattern and its cost in burnout, incidents, and missed learning.
Change recognition to reward prevention and durable fixes.
Add operational excellence goals to planning and reviews.
Coach leaders to stop praising avoidable heroics.
whyItWorks: Defines culture as repeated behavior under pressure.
Shows how the new behavior was sustained.
exampleStories.weakVersion: I told the organization we needed a more sustainable culture and encouraged managers to recognize preventive work.
followUpAngles: How did leaders model the change?
How did you know the culture shifted?

exampleStories.title: Blameful Incident Reviews
exampleStories.promptVariant: Describe a time when the existing culture was blocking technical progress.
exampleStories.situation: Incident reviews were nominally blameless but engineers avoided surfacing weak ownership, bad alerts, and risky shortcuts because leaders used reviews to find fault.
strongAnswerSketch: Identify the gap between stated values and actual behavior in reviews.
Redesign reviews around decision points, system conditions, and action ownership.
Model accountability by naming leadership misses first.
Track action completion and review quality over time.
whyItWorks: Changes the ritual where the culture is reinforced.
exampleStories.weakVersion: I reminded teams that our postmortems were blameless and asked managers to create psychological safety.
followUpAngles: What behavior showed the culture was unsafe?
What changed in the review format?

strongAnswerPattern.summary: The candidate shows culture diagnosis, incentive change, role modeling, and measurable behavioral shift.
moves: Defines culture as observed behavior under pressure.
Explains what incentives reinforced the old behavior.
Shows resistance and how it was handled.

weakAnswerPattern.summary: The candidate describes culture through values posters, slogans, or broad messaging without changing what leaders reward.
redFlags: Uses vague culture terms without behavior examples.
Has no evidence the culture changed under pressure.

followUps.question: What behavior told you the culture needed to change?
How did you personally **model the new behavior**?
How did you know the change sustained under pressure?

signals.name: Behavioral Diagnosis
signals.strong: Defines culture through observed behaviors and consequences.

signals.name: Incentive Design
signals.strong: Changes what leaders recognize, reward, and tolerate.

signals.name: Sustained Change
signals.strong: Shows the new behavior persisted during pressure.

rubric.expected: Changes team norms through behavior, feedback, and consistent expectations.
Changes cross-team rituals and incentives that shape engineering behavior.
Changes organizational culture through **leadership expectations**, operating cadence, and recognition systems.
Shapes company technology culture in ways that support strategy, trust, and sustainable execution.

prompts.label: What behavior pattern was blocking progress?
What culture shift were you accountable for?
What incentives, rituals, and leadership behaviors changed?
What behavior changed, and how did you know?
What did you learn about changing culture?
What mechanism sustained the new behavior?

relatedScenarios: Moving from founder-driven decisions to scalable ownership.
Building a culture of documentation in a remote organization.
